call.label: Police, fire, ambulance and sea rescue
Police, not urgent
call.note: Open around the clock. From abroad or on a foreign mobile, +46 77 114 14 00.

call.label: Poisons Information Centre, less urgent cases
call.note: Open day and night. In an acute case, call 112 and ask for poison information.

call_notes.text: A 112 call can reach the police, the fire service, an ambulance, sea, air and mountain rescue, poison information and social emergency services.
The poison centre does not take text messages.

alerts.text: An Important Public Announcement (in Swedish, VMA) is used when something serious has happened, such as a factory fire with toxic smoke or a risk of explosion. If it concerns the area you are in, follow the instructions at once.

It reaches you by radio and TV, by text message to phones used in the affected area, by SE-Alert, on krisinformation.se and its app, in the SR Play app and in the SOS Alarm 112 app. Sirens are used only for truly serious incidents.

SE-Alert is cell broadcast: every phone in the affected area gets a sharp signal, a vibration and a message on the screen, with no app and no sign-up. The phone must be an updated smartphone. Where needed, the alert can go out silently.
About 4,500 sirens stand on roofs and tall buildings across the country. They are tested at 3 pm on the first Monday (not a holiday) of March, June, September and December.

Siren signals. Important announcement: a 7-second blast, then a 14-second pause. Go indoors, close windows, doors and ventilation, and tune to Sveriges Radio P4. Air raid alarm: short blasts for one minute. Go to the nearest shelter or basement. All clear: one 30-second continuous blast.
Emergency alert (30-second blast, 15-second pause, for 5 minutes): the highest alert level for the whole country. Go indoors and listen to P4.
Weather warnings come from SMHI in three levels: yellow, orange and red, with red the most serious.

first_steps.text: Go indoors, close windows and doors, and put on Sveriges Radio P4 when you hear the important-announcement signal and it isn't a test.

Near a nuclear power station: the same signal means go indoors, close doors, windows and ventilation, and tune to P4. Homes in the emergency zones have a special warning receiver that sounds a loud alarm.
In an orange weather warning, avoid exposing yourself to the weather.

authorities.name: SOS Alarm
authorities.role: One of the services you reach when you call 112. It also passes on important public announcements and sends them as text messages.

authorities.name: Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency
authorities.role: Runs krisinformation.se, with information from Swedish authorities before, during and after a crisis.

authorities.name: Swedish Police
authorities.role: Police; 112 for urgent help, 114 14 for everything else.

authorities.name: SMHI (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute)
authorities.role: Monitors the weather and issues warnings.

authorities.name: Poisons Information Centre
authorities.role: Advice on poisoning, day and night.

hazards.text: Severe weather, with warnings from SMHI.
Accidents at the three nuclear power stations, each with its own warning sirens and household receivers in the emergency zones.
Ice floes in the waters around the country, especially the Gulf of Bothnia, can disrupt shipping.

climate.text: Temperate in the south, with cold, cloudy winters and cool, partly cloudy summers. Subarctic in the north.
